title: The Builder's Box Room
synopsis: Sofia comes with the city inspector.
Signor Valli smiles and says, "Search all you like!"
Three stones, one story that is not true, and one dropped pass.
goal: Find the real piece in Valli's office and prove what he did.

options.label: Stone A
options.feedback: This stone has a lion, not a street and an owl.
options.altText: a grey marble stone carved with a lion's head

options.label: Stone B
options.feedback: It has street lines. But look for the tiny owl and the crack.
options.altText: a grey marble stone carved with street lines, with no owl and no crack

options.label: Stone C
options.altText: a grey marble stone carved with street lines, a tiny owl and a crack shaped like a Y

notes: A picture choice with the names hidden: all three stones are grey marble of 12 kg, so the inspector's notes cannot tell them apart; Aldo's photo (recalled) can: a street, a tiny owl, a Y-shaped crack.
Stone C is the real piece's own picture (ev_real_piece); A and B are drawn from it so the three look alike but for their carvings.

The heavy box nobody may open.

play.title: Three Stones
story: Sofia arrives with the city inspector, a tall woman with a clipboard.
Signor Valli opens his office with a big smile. "Search all you like!"
In his box room, there are three grey stones on a shelf.
play.letter:
THE BOX ROOM — THREE STONES
All three are grey marble.
All three weigh about 12 kg.
Only one is the real map piece.
Check them against Aldo's photo.
play.question: Which stone is the real map piece?
hints: Open Aldo's photo. What marks does the real piece have?
Look at each stone for a tiny owl and a crack shaped like a Y.
transition: Livia touches the stone gently. "It is the real one."
Pia's stall is only two streets away.
Giulia runs to bring her here.

clue.title: The Real Piece
clue.note: The real map piece was in Valli's box room, next to a second plaster copy.

evidence.name: The Real Map Piece
evidence.description: The real piece of Rome's marble map, found in Valli's box room.
evidence.inscription: A long street, a tiny owl, and a crack shaped like a Y.

recall.title: Which one is real?
recall.prompt: Which thing in your Notebook shows the real piece's mark?
recall.miss: Find the old photo Aldo gave you.

lines.text: That old thing? It is mine!
I bought it last Sunday, at Campo de' Fiori.
A man called Leo sold it to me.
Then we will ask the flower seller.

discovery.title: THE REAL MAP PIECE
discovery.detail: The street, the owl and the Y crack, just like Aldo's photo.

options.label: The market is closed on Sunday.
Valli bought the stone there on Sunday.
options.feedback: Only Signor Valli says that. Find two people who agree.

options.label: Leo sells stones at the market.
options.feedback: Nobody else knows Leo. Compare the other answers about Sunday.

notes: Played as a talk (DialogueScene) in Valli's office: Pia and Sofia agree that the market is closed on Sunday, so Valli's story breaks. Pia's 'There is no Leo' is heard after (then) and is what Valli admits in the final.
Moved from Pia's stall to the site office: the three people it compares are there together.

clueInputs.note: Valli says he bought the stone at a market.
Pia keeps the flower stall at Campo de' Fiori.

learning.objective: 세 사람에게 시장에 대해 묻고, 일요일에 대해 두 사람이 일치하는 진술(closed on Sunday)을 찾아 Valli의 말이 거짓임을 밝힌다.
expressions: On Sunday, the square is empty.

play.title: A Market on Sunday?
story: Pia comes in with Giulia, her arms full of roses.
Signor Valli smiles, but his eyes do not.
Director Sofia stands by the window.
play.letter:
Signor Valli says he bought the stone at the market.
Ask everyone about the market.
Find two people who say the same thing about Sunday.
play.question: What is true about the market on Sunday?
hints: Ask everyone the same question about Sunday.
Two people agree. One person does not.
transition: The market is closed on Sunday. Nobody bought a stone there.
Pia waves a rose at Signor Valli. "You are not a good liar!"
The inspector takes out her notebook.

clue.title: The Closed Market
clue.note: Pia and Sofia say the market is closed on Sunday. And there is no Leo.

evidence.name: Pia's Answer
evidence.description: What Pia said about Signor Valli's story.
evidence.inscription: We are open every day from Monday to Saturday.

dialogue.goal: Is Signor Valli's market story true?

discovery.title: NO MARKET ON SUNDAY
discovery.detail: Signor Valli did not buy the stone. His story is not true.

play.title: Valli's Plan, Step by Step
story: The inspector puts every piece of evidence on Valli's desk.
"Detective," she says, "tell me what happened, in order."
play.letter:
THE GATE LOG: Thursday, 11:50 PM — a heavy box comes to the site.
THE LOAN BOOK: Tuesday, 2 PM — the real piece leaves the museum lab.
CARLA BASSI: Tuesday, 3 PM — a mould is made from the real piece.
ENZO: Thursday, 11:00 PM — Signor Valli "checks the lights" in the map hall.
play.question: Put Signor Valli's plan in order.
hints: Put the days first: Tuesday comes before Thursday.
On the same day, look at the times: 2 PM is before 3 PM.
transition: Tuesday: he took the piece and had a mould made. Thursday: he swapped in the copy and carried the real piece here.
Signor Valli is not smiling any more.
play.orderFeedback: Read the days and times again. Tuesday comes first.

clue.title: Valli's Plan
clue.note: Tuesday: loan and mould. Thursday: the swap at 11 PM, the site at 11:50 PM.

evidence.name: The Inspector's List

evidence.inscription: Tuesday: loan, mould. Thursday: swap, site.

discovery.title: THE PLAN, STEP BY STEP

notes: Recall: the museum pass Valli dropped on Thursday (Case 03). Letter: his confession, its last word left for the player.

clueInputs.note: The pass Valli dropped on Thursday night.
The car park on the city plan: what he would lose.
His market story was not true either.

learning.objective: 자백의 앞 문장들(땅값, 기계값)을 읽고 그가 잃기 싫었던 것을 단어로 완성한다.
expressions: If people saw it, the city would stop my car park.

play.title: The Pass He Dropped
story: "You have no proof I was at the museum on Thursday," says Signor Valli.
Then he sits down, very slowly.
play.letter:
"All right. There is no Leo.
That pass is mine. I dropped it on Thursday night.
I saw the library on the new piece, before the show.
If people saw it, the city would stop my car park.
I paid for the land. I paid for the machines.
I did not want to lose my . . . . ."
play.question: What did Signor Valli not want to lose? Spell it.
hints: He paid for the land and the machines. What do you pay with?
It is in your purse or your piggy bank.
play.successMessage: Signor Valli told the truth at last.
transition: The inspector closes her notebook. "The work stops. Now."
There will be no concrete tomorrow.
Livia holds the real piece like a baby bird.
play.orderFeedback: All five tiles fit. What do you pay with?

intro: It is the morning of 9 May. The concrete comes tomorrow.
Director Sofia arrives with the city inspector.
"Signor Valli," says the inspector, "we would like to see your office."
play.caseSummary: The real piece was in Valli's box room. It has the owl and the Y-shaped crack. Pia and Sofia agreed: the market is closed on Sunday. So Valli's story was not true. Step by step, the evidence showed his plan. Then the pass he dropped made him tell the truth. He did not want to lose his money.

notes: The culprit's reveal (mainMystery.revealCase). Every link of his plan was found earlier: s3_ep07_e4, s3_ep05_c3, s3_ep08_c3, s3_ep10_c3, s3_ep03_e4.
Valli is caught by evidence, not by a guess: the season's rule.

STEP 3-14: M1 is now a picture choice of three marble stones (Stone B is no longer a second plaster copy, which the detective already holds), M2 a talk with Valli, Pia and Sofia in the site office. Valli's site portrait is shown. Discovery Moments and an ending added.
